newsitem.title: UK: Brazil again dominates orders on sugar freight mkt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil again dominates orders on sugar freight mkt.

text.p: South Brazil once again accounted for most new business as an origin on London's sugar freight market at the start of the week, shipbrokers said on Monday.
Czarnikow Rionda had five orders from Latin American origins, mainly Brazil.

It quoted for 10/12,000 tonnes in bags from south Brazil to West Africa for prompt shipment and a further 14,000 from the same origin to west/east Africa with options of Red Sea and Colombo for prompt/seven days.
Rionda also quoted for 5,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santos to Luanda for prompt dates.
Its non-Brazil orders were 23,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Buenaventura to Black Sea for prompt/onwards and 7,000 in bags from Mazatlan or Manzanillo to west Africa for prompt dates.

Glencore quoted for 14/16,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Santos to Med/Black Sea for June 21/27 and CSC was open for around 26/27,000 tonnes from Puerto Quetzal to US Gulf/Atlantic for prompt shipment.
Shipbrokers said Genoc was open for 12,900/13,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maputo to Nantes for June 6/12.
Zimbabwe Sugar Sales was open for 14,000 tonnes in bulk, also from Maputo, to London for June 14/20. The last reported rate was close to $24, they said.
Secretan was open with a number of bagged sugar orders, from mainly European and Brazilian origins.
It quoted for 13,000 tonnes from Immingham to Mediterranean for June 16/25, 6,000 from Antwerp to Algeria for June 15/20 and 4,300 preslung from Gijon to Algeria for June 15/18.
Secretan was also open for 14/16,000 tonnes in bulk from Santos to Med/Black Sea for June 21/27 and 4/6,000 tonnes in bags from Santos to west Africa for June 10/15.
It quoted for 13/13,650 tonnes in bags from south China to Pakistan/Red Sea for June 10/15.

E D & F Man was in the market with a number of orders, quoting for 12,500 tonnes min/max in bags from Immingham to Tunisia for June 12/19 and 11,000 min/max bulk from Thailand to the Philippines for June 15/20.
U & B Shipping quoted an account order for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar Santos to Dar es Salaam with options of Mombasa, Yemen, Karachi, Colombo and Dubai for prompt/15 days notice.
It floated freight rate expectations of $36.00 basis east Africa, $36.50 for Dubai/Colombo and $37.00 for Karachi/Yemen.
More sugar account orders emerged from David Bruce, for 12,000 tonnes in bags from Paranagua to the Red Sea for June 13/17 and 10,000 from Rio de Janeiro to Egypt for June 15/25.

Masters Shipbroking quoted an account order for 4/6,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santos to Banjul and Tema for 10 days notice. Of the day's firmer business, Charterhouse Shipbroking said it was fully firm with 11,400 tonnes in bags from south China to Pakistan/Red Sea for June 15/20.
Cargill was said to have fixed 10,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Visakhaphatnam to the Mediterranean for prompt shipment.
Brazilian shippers SIMAB were saidto have fixed a prompt 25,000 tonnes Recife-Med/Black Sea for early June at around $30.
-- Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
